name: Sesriem Canyon
why: A short walk into a narrow gorge the Tsauchab river cut through layered conglomerate, cool and shaded under walls up to 30 m high.
book: Inside Namib-Naukluft National Park: buy the park permit at the office just inside the Sesriem gate. The canyon is about 4 km from the gate on a gravel road; the park closes at sunset.
water: Carry 1 litre; the pools in the canyon are not for drinking.
dangers: Never enter the canyon when rain clouds are over the Naukluft: flash floods.
Loose rock on the steps down and from the walls.
Hot from October to March: go late in the afternoon.
turnaround: Turn back at deep water or where the floor narrows into boulders; be out before sunset to leave the park in time.

points.name: Sesriem Canyon rim
points.note: Parking at the canyon edge. The name means 'six belts': Dorsland trekkers tied six rawhide thongs to lower a bucket to the water.

points.name: Steps down to the canyon floor
points.note: A short path and steps lead down into the gorge.

points.name: Sesriem Canyon floor
points.note: Sand and pebbles between walls of cemented gravel, about 500 m downstream of the steps. Walk back the same way.
